statusDetail: Completed atomic audit of 58 checks across home, article, scores, and error templates. Geographic routing resolved the entry URL to ESPN UK.

page.framework: React-like home and score surfaces with server-rendered editorial article HTML
page.notes: Public sports media site. The requested .com entry redirected to https://www.espn.co.uk/ under the audit network location. Not covered: authenticated Disney account, paid playback, checkout, account cancellation, or other external-domain flows.

paths.description: Entry/news-feed archetype and primary sports-discovery surface. Also tested consent, preferences, keyboard, network, performance, metadata, and no-JS rendering.
Representative editorial article template, covering reading, article semantics, structured metadata, imagery, mobile reflow, and no-JS content.
Representative live/listing and interactive scores template, covering navigation, dense data layout, mobile reflow, and repeated scrolling memory behaviour.
Representative failed route to assess HTTP/error recovery and navigation continuity.

findings.summary: ESPN ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the probe reports html color-scheme "normal" and body background rgb(237, 238, 240); the screenshot remains the light theme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven light/dark tokens using the dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not suppress active animation
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, document.getAnimations() still returned running 400ms animations and no preference media rules were found in accessible CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add prefers-reduced-motion overrides that remove non-essential transitions and auto-motion.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The feature is available in the browser, but the CSS probe found no view-transition rules and representative navigation swaps immediately.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document and cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route or score-state changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The consent wall obscures every primary surface on first load
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, article, scores, and 404 screenshots all open with a modal covering the page. On 360px it fills nearly the entire viewport and pushes the action row below the fold.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the initial copy, keep Accept and Reject equally prominent, fit all primary actions in the mobile viewport, and preserve accessible declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Dense side rails and repeated modules compete with the core feed
findings.evidence: The desktop homepage uses three columns with subscribe, customisation, topics, quick links, video, headlines, and multiple repeated rails around the primary story feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or collapse low-priority rails and give the primary news or score content a clearer dominant column.

findings.summary: Football scores force a 1000px desktop canvas into a 360px viewport
findings.evidence: The scores layout primitive reports innerWidth and scrollWidth 1000px with a 360px visual viewport, producing 640px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove desktop minimum widths, use intrinsic/fluid sizing, and recompose each fixture card into a narrow single-column layout.

findings.summary: Reused scoreboard components do not adapt at component level
findings.evidence: The score template remains 1000px wide at a 360px viewport and inspected computed styles report container-type normal rather than a component query context.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to score modules and use @container rules to switch fixture detail and action layouts at available-width thresholds.

findings.summary: Zoom is disabled and several visible controls are undersized
findings.evidence: The viewport is initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails meta-viewport. The probe found multiple visible links only 14–19px high and focus was only a 1px outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow pinch zoom, provide at least 24px minimum targets (prefer 44px for primary touch controls), and strengthen :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Mobile lab loading is slow despite a fast desktop trace
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 10.0s, TBT 820ms, performance 0.38, and TTI 27.5s. The desktop trace was much better at LCP 1.88s and TBT 32.64ms, showing a material mobile/device sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the mobile LCP chain, prioritise the hero, and delay non-critical scripts and modules until after content.

findings.summary: The entry page ships a large, redirect-heavy critical load
findings.evidence: HAR captured 182 requests and 3.64MB transferred, including 2.20MB script and 418KB CSS; Lighthouse reports 1.25s redirect savings and 179KB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate the espn.com to espn.co.uk redirect for regional entry, trim critical CSS, set durable caching, and prioritise only LCP-critical assets.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped CSS and JavaScript are unused
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,004KiB unused JavaScript and 199KiB unused CSS; HAR records 38 script requests with 8.36MB decoded script content.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by template, remove duplicate/legacy paths, and conditionally load advertising, account, and media code only when needed.

findings.summary: Many images lack text alternatives
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 85 of 100 homepage images and 10 of 14 article images without alt; Lighthouse fails image-alt on 42 nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful editorial images concise alt text and explicitly mark decorative icons with empty alt or CSS backgrounds.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail colour contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 34 colour-contrast failing nodes and an overall accessibility score of 0.86.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG contrast in default, hover, disabled, and dimmed states.

findings.summary: The page prevents user scaling
findings.evidence: The authored viewport explicitly sets maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no, which Lighthouse flags and which prevents users from zooming the dense news layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable=no, then test at 200% and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: The homepage logs browser errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails errors-in-console with four logged errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the four console errors and add regression monitoring so load-time exceptions fail CI.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs, inspector issues, and a BFCache blocker remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecation warning, inspector issues, legacy JavaScript, and a BFCache failure reason.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated APIs, fix DevTools Issues findings, remove unload/BFCache blockers, and stop serving avoidable legacy code.

findings.summary: Many navigation links are not crawlable or descriptive
findings.evidence: The homepage probe finds 87 href="#" anchors and 9 anchors without href; Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors and link-text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real destination href values for navigation and descriptive visible or accessible link names.

findings.summary: Transport hardening and cookie defaults are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows HTTPS and frame-ancestors CSP, but no HSTS or nosniff. Cookie evidence reports 10 of 11 cookies without Secure, all SameSite=None, and SWID lasting 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and nosniff, scope CSP beyond frame-ancestors, and set Secure plus Lax/Strict on cookies unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: The default page has a very large third-party and tracking footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence records 27 third-party origins including DoubleClick; HAR attributes 179 of 182 requests and 3.59MB to origins classified third-party, while the consent UI names 1017 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Load only essential providers before consent, reduce vendor count, batch analytics, and defer advertising integrations until a contextual choice.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced policies are absent
findings.evidence: The main response has no HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff; CSP only defines frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Set least-privilege Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, HSTS, nosniff, and a full nonce/hash-based CSP appropriate to the application.

findings.summary: The homepage’s current content is poorly represented without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability comparison finds only 29% word overlap between rendered and raw content and no matching raw title, while the article template preserves 84%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the current homepage headlines and primary navigation just as the article template server-renders its content.

findings.summary: An active service worker does not provide an observable offline cache
findings.evidence: The PWA probe finds a manifest and active service-worker.js registration but caches.keys() is empty, giving no evidence of an offline shell or fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a minimal offline shell and a useful offline response for saved/current content, with explicit stale and retry states.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate the resource budget
findings.evidence: HAR reports 3.59MB across 179 third-party-classified requests, including 2.20MB transferred script overall, before the user engages with video or account features.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer ad and account SDKs, and remove providers that do not demonstrate user value.

findings.summary: ESPN blocks major AI agents and offers no structured agent tools
findings.evidence: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, anthropic-ai, Google-Extended, CCBot, and others; the probe finds no WebMCP surface. This is an emerging opportunity, not a conventional SEO failure.
findings.suggestedFix: If ESPN wants agent reach, define an explicit licensed crawler policy and expose safe read-only search, scores, and article tools with WebMCP.

findings.summary: The scores page has a heavy steady-state heap
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 1,704,379 nodes and 96.3MB self size, including 90,611 closures, for a single scoreboard view.
findings.suggestedFix: Use heap retainers and allocation profiling to remove unnecessary objects/listeners and lazy-create below-fold score modules.

taskList.title: Reduce and defer the script, CSS, redirect, and third-party load
Restore zoom, target sizing, alt text, and colour contrast
Make the consent experience fit mobile without obscuring the task
Server-render current homepage content and real navigation hrefs
Fix console, deprecation, inspector, and BFCache issues
Clarify an agent-access strategy and optional structured tools
Reduce secondary chrome and add transitions where useful
